pages.text: A play shed stood at the end of the yard. The big ball was inside.
Lala wanted to play with the big ball. The dark shed made Lala's shoulders hunch.
Lala opened the door only a palm's width, holding the handle tightly with one hand.
Lala reached the other hand through the gap. "Too dark to go in." Fingertips could almost touch the ball.
When the handle slipped away, the door slammed shut. The ball rolled farther inside.
The children waited in a circle in the middle of the yard. The shed door was tightly closed.
Lala stood before them empty-handed. Those fingertips still trembled.
Teacher Bau stood at the shed door. "Lala, what comes in if you open the door all the way?"
Lala pushed the door wide open. Sunlight reached right across the shed floor.
Lala came out hugging the big ball. The children kicked it again and again.
